note: Option lists of the character creator (CharacterCreator, CreatorOptions). Faces, skin, eyes and hair come from assets/character/body/peoples.json; this file adds facial hair, eyebrows, markings and jewellery, and which of them each people offers. Period notes follow the costume bible (Player_Animation_Project/graph_analysis/customizer/costume_bible.md): men were usually clean-shaven (1.3), Eastern Woodlands men plucked their beards (3.4), smallpox pitting and scars are authentic details (1.2), tattoos, clan emblems and paint other than the documented women's vermilion cheek spots are left out until designed with the nations concerned (3.6). The same rules apply to every people; option lists differ only where a documented custom differs.

stylized.label: Stylized
stylized.note: Painted, sculpted faces in a heroic game style: bolder forms, larger eyes, hand-painted skin and hair. The same stylization for every people; each face keeps its own features.

realistic.label: Realistic
realistic.note: The anatomical faces: skin with pores and fine detail, strand-shaded hair and brows.

lined.label: Lined
lined.note: A few painted lines of expression and weather.

weathered.label: Weathered
weathered.note: Deeper lines and a ruddier, sun-worn tone: years outdoors.

plucked.label: Plucked
plucked.note: Eastern Woodlands men plucked the beard with brass-wire tweezers (costume bible 3.4).

stubble.label: Stubble
stubble.note: A week or more without a razor.

sideburns.label: Side whiskers
sideburns.note: Hair left in front of the ears.

moustache_thin.label: Thin moustache
moustache_thin.note: A light moustache over a shaved face.

moustache.label: Moustache
moustache.note: Worn by some soldiers and by many men of the Ottoman and South Asian worlds.

moustache_sideburns.label: Moustache and side whiskers
moustache_sideburns.note: A moustache with the hair in front of the ears left.

chin_beard.label: Moustache and chin beard
chin_beard.note: The cheeks shaved, the chin and lip left.

chin_curtain.label: Beard without moustache
chin_curtain.note: Kept by some Anabaptist (Amish, Mennonite) men among the German settlers of Pennsylvania while most men shaved (grade C, artistic licence).

beard_short.label: Short beard
beard_short.note: Unusual in the colonies; a long scout or a captivity left men bearded.

beard_full.label: Full beard
beard_full.note: Rare among colonists in the 1750s; common among older men of West Asia, North Africa and Korea.

pox.label: Smallpox scars
pox.note: Pitting from smallpox, common in every people of the period; the ranger Jacob was described with it (costume bible 1.2).

vermilion_cheeks.label: Vermilion cheek spots
vermilion_cheeks.note: Women's dress: a round spot of vermilion on each cheek (Zeisberger; costume bible 3.3 and 3.6).

ear_bobs_silver.label: Silver ear bobs
ear_bobs_silver.note: Ball-and-cone ear bobs of trade silver (costume bible 3.2).

ear_bobs_several.label: Silver ear bobs, several
ear_bobs_several.note: Several ear bobs in each ear (Jones, 1773; costume bible 3.3).

nose_jewel_silver.label: Silver nose jewel
nose_jewel_silver.note: A small silver pendant from the nose (Shawnee, 1773; costume bible 3.2).

ring_one_ear.label: Ring in one ear
ring_one_ear.note: Colonial advertisements describe some men with a ring in one ear.

japanese.note_jewellery: Pierced ears were not worn in Edo Japan.

korean.note_jewellery: Joseon custom discouraged pierced ears after 1572.

vietnamese.note_jewellery: Vietnamese women wore earrings; men usually wore none.

malay.note_jewellery: Malay women wore ear studs; men usually wore none.

pacific_islander.note_jewellery: Islanders of both sexes wore pearls, flowers or feathers in their ears. Tatau (tattooing) is left out until designed with the peoples concerned.

persian.note_jewellery: Pearls from the Gulf's banks were worn in Iran and Arabia.

arab.note_jewellery: Bedouin and village women wore a nose ring with their earrings; pearls came from the Gulf.

kurdish.note_jewellery: Kurdish women often wore a gold nose ring with their earrings.

egyptian.note_jewellery: Egyptian village women wore a nose ring, as travellers recorded.

ethiopian.note_jewellery: Highland women wore silver earrings; men usually wore none.

emblems.note: Original line emblems drawn by PeopleEmblem (scripts/customizer/people_emblem.gd): a plant, landscape or craft of each people's homeland, one ink colour on the same roundel for every people. No flags, heraldry, religious or sacred symbols, clan emblems, wampum, regalia or depictions of people.
emblems.scots_irish: Flax in flower (the Ulster linen trade)
emblems.french: Wheat sheaf (the habitant farms of the St Lawrence)
emblems.haudenosaunee: Longhouse (the bark house of the Six Nations' towns)
emblems.lenape: River through a gap in the ridges (the Delaware)
emblems.shawnee: Wooded hills of the Ohio country
emblems.african_american: Coiled basket (the coiled grass baskets made in the colonies from African practice)
emblems.vietnamese: Rice seedlings in a flooded paddy
emblems.spanish: Bitter oranges (the orange groves of Seville and Valencia)
emblems.ethiopian: Coffee branch (the highlands where coffee first grew)
emblems.ottoman_turkish: Tulip (the Tulip Era, a motif of Iznik tiles)
emblems.persian: Cypress (the sarv of Persian gardens and carpets)
emblems.arab: Dhow (the trading ship of the Red Sea and the Gulf)
emblems.moorish: Horseshoe arch (the gates of Morocco's towns)
